inputs.question: In low- and middle-income countries, do programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities work, and which kinds work best?
inputs.scope:
Covers: Programmes or interventions in low- and middle-income countries aimed at improving educational outcomes (access, enrolment, attendance, retention, completion, learning or academic achievement, and transition) for children and young people with physical, sensory, intellectual, developmental or psychosocial disabilities. It also covers what the evidence says about which types of intervention perform comparatively better.
Out of scope:
- Effectiveness of disability-education programmes in high-income countries (The question is restricted to low- and middle-income settings, where school systems, resources and evidence bases differ substantially.)
- How many children with disabilities are out of school or the size of the education gap (That is a prevalence and description question, not a question about whether interventions work.)
- Health, rehabilitation or functional outcomes of interventions (e.g., mobility, vision correction itself) (Only educational outcomes are in scope; health gains are relevant only insofar as they translate into educational outcomes.)
- Whether inclusive education is a human-rights obligation (That is a normative and legal question; this page addresses empirical effectiveness.)
- Detailed cost-effectiveness or budget comparisons across programmes (Cost data are rarely reported alongside effects. The page will note cost evidence only where it is directly reported, not build an economic analysis.)

Covers: Programmes or interventions in low- and middle-income countries aimed at improving educational outcomes (access, enrolment, attendance, retention, completion, learning or academic achievement, and transition) for children and young people with physical, sensory, intellectual, developmental or psychosocial disabilities. It also covers what the evidence says about which types of intervention perform comparatively better.
Out of scope:
- Effectiveness of disability-education programmes in high-income countries (The question is restricted to low- and middle-income settings, where school systems, resources and evidence bases differ substantially.)
- How many children with disabilities are out of school or the size of the education gap (That is a prevalence and description question, not a question about whether interventions work.)
- Health, rehabilitation or functional outcomes of interventions (e.g., mobility, vision correction itself) (Only educational outcomes are in scope; health gains are relevant only insofar as they translate into educational outcomes.)
- Whether inclusive education is a human-rights obligation (That is a normative and legal question; this page addresses empirical effectiveness.)
- Detailed cost-effectiveness or budget comparisons across programmes (Cost data are rarely reported alongside effects. The page will note cost evidence only where it is directly reported, not build an economic analysis.)
